A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WildCap and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–B. The retained material can be matched reliably despite added appendix sections and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments, including the six-subject quantitative comparison in Table 1, component ablations, and smartphone and NeRSemble results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds a synthetic Digital Emily evaluation in Table 2 and further qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and Appendix A retain the SwitchLight preprocessing, masked texel-grid lighting, joint seven-channel diffusion sampling, losses, initialization, and super-resolution procedure. The revised albedo-focused wording does not establish an algorithm change. The new mask-editing example investigates the existing manually supplied mask.

E1.justification: Appendix B.4 adds evaluation on synthetic multiview images rendered from the Digital Emily scan, previously only cited. Figure 15 also adds SwitchLight processing of example subjects from Xu et al. and Rainer et al. The training scans, smartphone captures, and NeRSemble demonstrations remain.

E2.justification: The evaluated external comparators remain SwitchLight, FLARE, DeFace, their processed-input variants, and DoRA. Digital Emily reuses DeFace* and FLARE*. The new discussion of Xu et al. and Rainer et al. does not report running their methods against WildCap under matched conditions.

E3.justification: The added Digital Emily experiment compares reconstructed diffuse albedo with ground truth in image space using PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS on a common cropped facial region. This supplements the retained Table 1 protocol comparing rendered images with SwitchLight predictions. Figure 13 adds modified-mask and whole-face-lighting controls; existing experimental settings are otherwise retained.

E4.justification: Appendix B.3/Figure 13 adds a targeted analysis of mole removal within shadows, testing exclusion from the shadow mask and applying texel-grid lighting across the entire face. Appendix B.6/Figure 15 adds a SwitchLight case study on prior works' example subjects. Existing grid-size, component, skin-tone, and sharp-shadow analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Table 1 retains averaging over six subjects; the added Table 2 introduces no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 values are unchanged. New Table 2 reports PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS of 28.71/0.9802/0.0388 for WildCap, 28.43/0.9791/0.0826 for DeFace*, and 22.48/0.9742/0.0571 for FLARE*. These are additional synthetic results, not same-setting performance changes. Figures 13 and 15 add qualitative findings. Section 4.1 removes the unquantified claim that exponential scheduling slightly outperforms constant scheduling.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(12), the lighting representation, diffusion updates, regularizers, and Lambertian and supplied-skin-tone assumptions are retained. The added appendix analysis introduces no new formal definitions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion narrow the headline emphasis from facial appearance or reflectance capture to diffuse-albedo capture, explicitly describing other reflectance maps as predicted from albedo. The hybrid-rendering and texel-grid contributions and claimed quality gap reduction remain.

C2.justification: Appendix B.3 adds a specific limitation: default texel-grid lighting can absorb a mole into shading when its spatial scale resembles the grid. It attributes this to insufficient global context and explains mask exclusion as a mitigation. The existing sharp-shadow failure and preprocessing dependencies remain; the studio-dataset future direction is retained in Appendix B.5.

D1.justification: The abstract and introduction change code availability from a promised release to a reported release, and Section 4 adds a project-page link for supplementary material. Section 4.1 drops the iPhone X capture-device identification. Appendix B.3 adds practical mask-editing guidance; the existing hyperparameters, GPU information, and Appendix A implementation details remain.

R1.justification: New Appendix B.6 explicitly positions WildCap as addressing stronger cast shadows than examples from Xu et al. and Rainer et al., supplementing the earlier explanation that their code was unavailable. Section 3.1 also adds the HACK citation. Most related-work discussion and cited works are unchanged.

P1.justification: The revision edits the title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion around albedo capture, adds acknowledgements, and expands Appendix B with analysis, synthetic evaluation, and positioning subsections. Existing method and experimental prose largely remains, with local shortening and explanation changes rather than extensive restructuring.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 2 and Figures 13 and 15. The earlier NeRSemble and failure-case figures are retained as Figures 14 and 16. Several captions are revised or shortened, with accompanying page reflow; the original figure artwork and Table 1 structure remain.

improvement.justification: Table 2 adds direct ground-truth albedo validation to v1's comparison against SwitchLight-derived images, while Figure 13 documents a concrete detail-loss failure and mitigation. The narrower headline claims better reflect what is directly optimized. These gains are limited by the single-scan quantitative test and indirect closed-source comparisons, but outweigh the small loss of capture-device detail.
